asks.q: why is the start always so mad
a: cold tyres, cold brakes, full fuel tank and 20 people who all think they can make the same gap work
it's the only moment of the race where everyone is genuinely equal

asks.q: does the start decide the race
a: more than anyone admits
track position is everything on most circuits, you lose 3 places on lap 1 and you spend the next hour stuck behind someone slower

msgs: lap 2 was the busiest of the whole race

asks.q: why do they all overtake at the same time
a: because they all pitted around the same time
you come out on new tyres next to someone on old ones and it's basically a free pass. it stacks up
a flap on the rear wing that opens on the straights and makes the car faster
you only get it if you're within a second of the car ahead at a certain point. it's an artificial help to make passing possible
purists hate it. i'm fine with it, the alternative was processions

msgs: this is where it actually got decided btw
not a single overtake involved, just people stopping at different times

asks.q: why not just stop early every time
a: new tyres are quick for about 3 laps, then they start going off
stop too early and you're on dead rubber at the end with everyone hunting you. stop too late and someone's already jumped you
you pit before the guy ahead, do two really fast laps on new tyres while he's still out there on old ones
when he finally stops he comes out behind you. you never passed him on track, you passed him in the pit lane
